items.headline: Inflation Concerns Drive Broad Market Declines
items.summary: U.S. equities closed lower today, pulling Wall Street further from its recent record highs. Hotter-than-expected September Consumer Price Index (CPI) data fueled concerns over accelerating inflation, increasing the likelihood of another Federal Reserve interest rate hike this month. This economic data, coupled with mixed bank earnings and weakness in healthcare and financial sectors, dampened overall market sentiment. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Dell Technologies Sinks on Downgrade
items.summary: Dell Technologies ($DELL) shares lost 8.28% after Barclays downgraded the company, citing elevated valuations and a lack of significant enterprise AI-driven growth thus far.

items.headline: Progressive Misses Q3 Revenue Estimates
items.summary: The Progressive Corp. ($PGR) fell 8.01% today after the insurer reported third-quarter 2026 results that came in below Wall Street's revenue expectations.

items.headline: Bank of America Slumps After Profit Miss and Fine
items.summary: Bank of America ($BAC) shares dropped 7.5% following a report of weaker-than-expected third-quarter profit and revenue, compounded by a $1.2 billion Treasury fine over anti-money laundering shortcomings.

items.headline: BlackRock Rises on Strong Earnings
items.summary: BlackRock ($BLK) advanced 3% today after the investment management company reported stronger-than-expected profit and revenue for the summer, with customers pouring a net $205 billion into its funds.

items.headline: Meta Platforms Posts Gains
items.summary: Meta Platforms ($META) saw a 2.6% increase today, contributing to market movements.

items.headline: Nvidia Continues Upward Trend
items.summary: Nvidia ($NVDA) gained 1.0% today, reflecting continued investor interest in semiconductor and AI-related stocks.

items.headline: September CPI Exceeds Expectations, Fueling Rate Hike Bets
items.summary: The September U.S. Consumer Price Index (CPI) report showed headline inflation rising 0.6% month-over-month, bringing the annual rate to 3.7%, higher than the anticipated 3.6%. Core CPI, excluding food and energy, also surpassed forecasts, rising 0.3% monthly and 2.6% annually. This data has nearly doubled trader expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike at its upcoming meeting.

items.headline: Healthcare and Financials Lead Sector Declines; Energy Outperforms
items.summary: Six of the S&P 500's eleven broad sectors closed in the red today. The Health Care Select Sector SPDR (XLV) declined 1.3%, and the Financials Select Sector SPDR (XLF) fell 0.4%, as investors reacted to mixed bank earnings and disappointing guidance from healthcare companies. In contrast, the Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) advanced 1.7%, benefiting from mixed oil prices and ongoing supply concerns.

items.headline: Bank Earnings Offer Mixed Signals Amid Rising Yields
items.summary: Major U.S. banks reported mixed quarterly earnings, with firms like Bank of America ($BAC) experiencing declines due to profit misses and regulatory fines, while BlackRock ($BLK) posted strong results. Investors are increasingly scrutinizing forward guidance amidst a flattening yield curve and rising Treasury yields, which jumped after the inflation report.

items.headline: Semiconductor Stocks Under Pressure
items.summary: Technology and semiconductor stocks faced selling pressure today, contributing to the Nasdaq's decline. Concerns about AI competition and weak market breadth impacted firms like ASML, whose U.S. shares were down despite reporting record sales and strong profits.
